name: Every ranked briefing row names the bar its distance was measured from
notes: UPDATED (one snapshot per date) by developer: step 4 re-pins from 2026-07-25 to 2026-06-22. This step's whole point is the legacy-absence proof -- clicking a snapshot recorded BEFORE goal-desk-iter-9 added basis_as_of/basis_age_days, so step 5 can assert 'basis not recorded in this snapshot'. 2026-07-25 carried two recordings; the one-time cleanup kept the newer screen-2026-07-25-bd0b37ebc426, which DOES carry the basis fields, so that date can no longer prove the absence. screen-2026-06-22-3ecd45c062c7 is the only surviving pre-disclosure snapshot (10 ranked rows, no basis_as_of key at all) and was unpaired, so the cleanup left it untouched. Same assertion, a date that can still honestly make it. The click target also moves from the retired `desk-history-row` <tr> to the calendar's `desk-history-day` cell, which carries the same `data-screen-date` attribute.
Added goal-desk-iter-10 (documentation tidy-up, no behavior change; demo_runner.py's script validator ignores unknown top-level keys such as this one).

Steps 3 and 6 both assert text on the LATEST recorded screen's basis cell ('d before as-of'). Both REQUIRE the replay target's latest recorded screen snapshot to already carry basis_as_of/basis_age_days -- i.e. it must have been computed after the goal-desk-iter-9 J-08 change landed. A replay against a store whose latest screen predates that change fails steps 3 and 6 for an environmental reason (stale fixture/store state), not a product regression.

Steps 4 and 5 click a history row for a specific date (2026-07-25 in this script) and expect the honest legacy fallback. This REQUIRES that date to have EXACTLY ONE recorded screen snapshot in the replay target's store. apps/frontend/app/desk/page.tsx's handleSelectHistoryScreen fetches GET /research/desk/screen?date=<date> by DATE ONLY, never by unique snapshot id; desk_routes.py's get_screen resolves that query to the LAST matching record by created_utc (matching[-1]). If a SECOND screen is ever recorded for the same screen_date (the same-date screen ambiguity carried, not fixed, per docs/goal.md's NOTES), clicking EITHER history row for that date displays whichever snapshot is newest -- so steps 4 and 5 fail against a target where 2026-07-25 has more than one recorded snapshot, again an environmental/data-shape reason, not a product regression. Discovered empirically in goal-desk-iter-10: computing a fresh screen_date=2026-07-25 snapshot inside a scoped copy that already held the pre-existing legacy screen-2026-07-25-e184a7dc2f86 reproduced exactly this collision. See reports/phase-goal-desk-iter-10-j08-replay-results.md for the observed failure and docs/handoffs/goal-desk-iter-10-dev.md for the root-cause writeup.
